'''''Sedum rubrotinctum''''' or '''''Sedum'' × ''rubrotinctum''''', commonly known as '''jelly-beans''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> '''jelly bean plant''', or '''pork and beans''',<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-05-13 |title=Sedum rubrotinctum "Pork and Beans" {{!}} Succulents and Sunshine |url=https://www.succulentsandsunshine.com/types-of-succulents/sedum-rubrotinctum-pork-and-beans/ |access-date=2024-05-16 |website=www.succulentsandsunshine.com |language=en-US}}</ref> is a species of ''[[Sedum]]'' from the plant family [[Crassulaceae]]. It is a [[succulent plant]] originating in Mexico.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.plantcare.com/encyclopedia/jelly-bean-890.aspx |title=Jelly Bean – Sedum rubrotinctum – Indoor House Plants – Plant Encyclopedia Database at |publisher=Plantcare.com |date=2007-10-25 |accessdate=2010-04-27 |archive-date=2014-07-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140730145901/http://www.plantcare.com/encyclopedia/jelly-bean-890.aspx |url-status=dead }}</ref> The common English name refers to its short leaves that resemble [[jelly bean]]s, especially when taking on a protective hue.<ref name="Backyard Gardener"/> 

==Description==
[[File:Granite cliff with pink jelly bean plant and common houseleek.jpg|thumb|On granite cliff]]
[[File:Sedum Rubrotinctum potted plant.jpg|thumbnail|right]] 
The leaves of ''Sedum rubrotinctum'' change colour from green to red during the summer months as a protective adaptation.<ref name="Backyard Gardener"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.desert-tropicals.com/Plants/Crassulaceae/Sedum_rubrotinctum.html |title=Pork and Beans (Sedum rubrotinctum) |publisher=Desert-tropicals.com |date= |accessdate=2010-04-27 |archive-date=2012-03-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120319195342/http://www.desert-tropicals.com/Plants/Crassulaceae/Sedum_rubrotinctum.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> The plant sprouts bright yellow flowers from between the leaves in mid-spring.<ref name="Backyard Gardener">{{cite web|url=https://www.backyardgardener.com/plantname/sedum-rubrotinctum-pork-and-beans/|title=Sedum rubrotinctum (Pork and Beans) |publisher=Backyardgardener.com |date= |accessdate=2010-04-27}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
The species was first described in 1948. It is considered to be an artificial hybrid between ''[[Sedum pachyphyllum]]'' and ''[[Sedum stahlii]]''.<ref name=POWO_275989-1>{{Cite POWO|title=''Sedum'' × ''rubrotinctum'' R.T.Clausen|id=275989-1|access-date=2023-07-24|mode=cs1}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
''Sedum rubrotinctum'' is cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]], for planting in gardens and as potted plants. It is grown very easily and tolerates all types of soil except for those that are poorly drained. It grows very well in summer, can take variations in climate, although it is not frost-tolerant.

New plants may be grown from leaves (or beans) that drop off or are separated from the stem and laid on soil.

This plant has won the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/16987/Sedum-x-rubrotinctum/Details | title = ''Sedum'' × ''rubrotinctum'' | website = www.rhs.org | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 5 March 2021}}</ref>

''Sedum rubrotinctum'' is poisonous and may cause irritation when ingested or touched.<ref name="Backyard Gardener"/>
